name: Log odds ratio from a 2x2 table and its variance
expression: ln OR = ln( a*d / (b*c) ) ;  Var(ln OR) = 1/a + 1/b + 1/c + 1/d ;  if any cell = 0: a,b,c,d += 0.5 (that study only)
variables: a = events in the intervention arm; b = non-events in the intervention arm; c = events in the control arm; d = non-events in the control arm; ln OR = log odds ratio.
notes: [ext] The note-taker added this standard formula; the book shows only the numbers. Stata admetan and MetaXL add 0.5 only in studies with a zero cell, which matches the engine defaults (cc=0.5, cc_to='only0'). Check: T22 (2/94 vs 0/52) gives OR = (2.5*52.5)/(92.5*0.5) = 2.8378378 and SE = 1.5588003.

name: Log risk ratio from a 2x2 table and its variance
expression: ln RR = ln[ (a/n1) / (c/n2) ] ;  Var(ln RR) = 1/a - 1/n1 + 1/c - 1/n2
variables: a, c = events in the intervention and control arms; n1 = a + b and n2 = c + d = arm totals; ln RR = log risk ratio.
notes: [ext] Standard formula; ln RR is the effect metric of every Ch 12 plot and test. The zero-cell correction changes the magnesium LFK index (0.5 vs 1.0), so state which correction you used.

name: Standard error from a reported 95% CI of a ratio measure
expression: se = ( ln UCI - ln LCI ) / ( 2 * PHI^-1(0.975) ) = ( ln UCI - ln LCI ) / 3.919928
variables: UCI, LCI = upper and lower 95% confidence limits of the ratio (RR/OR/HR); PHI^-1(0.975) = invnormal(0.975) = 1.959964; se = standard error of the log ratio.
notes: Call conversions.se_from_ci with log_scale=True. The reference category (RR = 1, CI 1–1) gives se = 0, so the weight 1/se^2 is missing in Stata. REMR then gives that row the study's maximum weight.

name: SE of an arm mean (continuous dose-response data)
expression: sterr = sd / sqrt(n) ;  weight = 1 / sterr^2
variables: sd = standard deviation of the outcome in a dose category; n = number of patients in the category; sterr = standard error of the category mean.
notes: engine_ref is null: the engine implements only the inverse direction (conversions.sd_from_se, sd = se*sqrt(n)), not sterr from sd or the weight. The book uses sterr to weight absolute mean scores in REMR and to build the variance of the mean differences.

name: Within-study mean difference versus the reference dose and its variance
expression: d_ij = mean_ij - mean_0j ;  Var(d_ij) = sd_ij^2/n_ij + sd_0j^2/n_0j ;  Var(d_0j) = missing
variables: j = study; i = non-reference dose category; 0 = reference category (dose 0); mean, sd, n = category mean, SD and size; d_ij = mean difference against the reference.
notes: The Stata code computes s_pooled = sqrt(sterr_ij^2 + sterr_0j^2). The d_ij within a study share the reference arm, so they are correlated: Cov(d_ij, d_kj) = sd_0j^2/n_0j [ext]. REMR handles this with cluster-robust SEs. The book gives no SMD formulas and points only to Hedges' g and Cohen's d.

name: Assigned dose for an exposure interval
expression: dose_c = (L_c + U_c) / 2   (default) ;  alternatives: study-reported median or mean of category c
variables: L_c, U_c = lower and upper bounds of exposure category c; dose_c = dose assigned to the category.
notes: Nonparametric rule, because usually only the two bounds are known (Bekkering 2008; Takahashi & Tango 2010). The book does not say how to handle open-ended categories (e.g. '>= L4' in Table 13.1).

name: Fixed-effect model and inverse-variance pooled estimate
expression: theta_hat_j ~ N(mu, sigma_j^2) ;  mu_hat_FE = SUM w_j*theta_hat_j / SUM w_j ,  w_j = 1/v_j ;  Var(mu_hat_FE) = 1 / SUM w_j
variables: theta_hat_j = effect estimate of study j (log scale for ratios); sigma_j^2 = v_j = its within-study variance; mu = common true effect; w_j = inverse-variance weight.
notes: The book states only the distributional model; the pooled-estimate formulas are standard [ext]. In the engine use model='fixed'. Funnel plots in Ch 12 are always centred on mu_hat_FE.

name: Random-effects model
expression: theta_hat_j ~ N(theta_j, sigma_j^2) ;  theta_j ~ N(mu, tau^2)
variables: theta_j = true effect of study j; mu = mean of the true effects; tau^2 = between-study variance; sigma_j^2 = within-study variance.
notes: Thompson & Sharp 1999. The book gives no tau^2 estimator formula; the examples use DerSimonian–Laird through admetan. [note: Cochrane Handbook v6 prefers REML or Paule–Mandel to DL.]

name: IVhet pooled estimate and variance
expression: mu_hat_IVhet = mu_hat_FE ;  Var(mu_hat_IVhet) = SUM_j (w_j/SUM w)^2 * (v_j + tau2_DL) ;  CI = mu_hat +/- 1.96*SE
variables: w_j = 1/v_j = fixed-effect weight; v_j = within-study variance; tau2_DL = DerSimonian–Laird between-study variance; SE = sqrt(Var).
notes: [ext, verified] Reproduces IHDChol OR 0.825 (0.719, 0.946), z = -2.750, p = 0.006 exactly. Public entry point: models.meta_analysis(model='ivhet'). The robust no-covariate WLS regression reproduces only the point estimate (CI 0.760–0.895). [note: IVhet is the authors' own model. The Cochrane Handbook v6 default is a random-effects model with REML or Paule–Mandel τ², with an HKSJ CI when there are few studies.]

name: Cochran's Q (book: 'total variance')
expression: Q = SUM_j w_j * (theta_hat_j - theta_hat_FE)^2 ;  df = k - 1
variables: w_j = 1/v_j; theta_hat_FE = fixed-effect pooled estimate (or the model prediction in a meta-regression); k = number of studies.
notes: The book describes Q as the weighted sum of squared distances between observed and predicted values, and calls it the 'total variance', although it is not a variance. IHDChol: Q = 49.69, df = 27, p = 0.005. admetan labels this line 'Mantel-Haenszel Q'.

name: Modified H^2 (Stata)
variables: Q = Cochran's Q; df = k - 1; I^2 = Higgins' I^2 as a proportion.
notes: [ext, verified] IHDChol: (49.69 - 27)/27 = 0.840 and I^2 = 45.7%. The engine's models.heterogeneity reports the classical H2 = Q/df, so the modified H2 = H2 - 1; do not compare the two directly.

name: Robust (HC1 sandwich) variance of WLS coefficients
expression: V_rob(b) = N/(N - p) * (X'WX)^-1 [ SUM_j w_j^2 * e_j^2 * x_j x_j' ] (X'WX)^-1 ;  tests: t with N - p df
variables: X = design matrix (rows x_j; intercept plus covariates); W = diag(w_j), w_j = 1/SE_j^2 (fixed-effect weights); e_j = WLS residual; N = number of observations (studies); p = number of coefficients.
notes: [ext] Stata regress ... [aw=1/SE^2], vce(robust) (Huber–Eicker–White; Hedges, Tipton & Johnson 2010). The result does not change when the weights are rescaled (Stata rescales aweights to sum to N). Reproduces OR 0.6217 (0.5205, 0.7426) per unit of cholesterol reduction. Not implemented in the engine. [note: HC-type SEs are anti-conservative when there are few studies, and robust-error WLS meta-regression is a minority approach; the consensus is random-effects meta-regression with REML τ² and Knapp–Hartung tests.]

name: Cluster-robust variance (REMR)
expression: V_cl(b) = G/(G - 1) * (N - 1)/(N - p) * (X'WX)^-1 [ SUM_g u_g u_g' ] (X'WX)^-1 ,  u_g = SUM_{j in g} w_j e_j x_j ;  tests: t with G - 1 df
variables: G = number of clusters (studies); N = number of dose-specific observations; p = number of coefficients (constant plus spline terms); w_j = inverse-variance weight (reference rows get the study maximum); e_j = residual; x_j = design row.
notes: [ext] Stata regress ... [aweight=wt], vce(cluster id). 5 clusters give 4 df and 4 clusters give 3 df. Unstable with very few clusters. Not implemented in the engine.

name: Classical (random-effects) meta-regression model
expression: theta_hat_j = mu + beta_1*x_1j + ... + beta_i*x_ij + b_j + eps_j ;  eps_j ~ (0, sigma_j^2) ;  b_j ~ (0, tau^2) ;  WLS weights 1/(sigma_j^2 + tau^2)
variables: x_ij = study-level covariate i of study j; beta_i = regression coefficients; mu = constant; b_j = between-study ('non-random') error; eps_j = within-study error; tau^2 = residual between-study variance.
notes: [R] Rebuilt from scrambled fragments. With no covariates it reduces to theta_hat_j = mu + b_j + eps_j, whose tau^2 is tau2_0. The book fits it by WLS.

name: Residual tau^2, method of moments (DL-type) for meta-regression
expression: tau2_res = max{ 0, ( Q_E - (k - p) ) / tr(P) } ;  P = W - W X (X'WX)^-1 X'W ;  Q_E = SUM_j w_j (theta_hat_j - x_j' b_FE)^2
variables: W = diag(1/v_j); X = design matrix; b_FE = fixed-effect WLS coefficients; Q_E = residual heterogeneity statistic; k = number of studies; p = number of coefficients.
notes: [ext] Stata metareg ..., mm; equals metafor rma(method='DL', mods=...). Use the engine with tau2_method='DL'. IHDChol: tau2_res = 0.01647, Q_E = 37.87 on 26 df.

name: Knapp–Hartung adjusted coefficient variance
expression: Var_KH(b) = s^2 * (X'W*X)^-1 ,  s^2 = SUM_j w*_j (theta_hat_j - x_j' b)^2 / (k - p) ,  w*_j = 1/(v_j + tau^2) ;  tests: t with k - p df
variables: b = random-effects WLS coefficients; w*_j = random-effects weight; k = number of studies; p = number of coefficients.
notes: [ext] Neither the book nor the notes print this formula; it is the standard Knapp & Hartung (2003) form, which metareg applies by default. Use the engine with test='knha'. IHDChol: OR 0.594 (0.401, 0.881), p = 0.012.

name: Residual I^2 after meta-regression
expression: I2_res = ( Q_E - df_res ) / Q_E ,  df_res = k - p
variables: Q_E = residual heterogeneity Q of the fixed-effect meta-regression; k = number of studies; p = number of coefficients.
notes: [ext, verified] IHDChol: (37.87 - 26)/37.87 = 31.34%, which metareg labels '% residual variation due to heterogeneity'. The engine computes tau2/(tau2 + s2), which equals this formula when tau2_method='DL'.

name: Book's non-standard 'I^2_model' from the F statistic
expression: I2_model = ( F_model - df_r ) / F_model
variables: F_model = overall F statistic of the robust WLS regression; df_r = residual degrees of freedom.
notes: [R] Example: (30.23 - 26)/30.23 = 13.99%. This is not Higgins' I^2 and disagrees with I2_res = 31.34%. Kept only to recognise and flag it; do not use it.

name: R^2 analog: proportion of between-study variance explained
expression: R^2 = max[ (tau2_0 - tau2_model) / tau2_0 , 0 ]
variables: tau2_0 = between-study variance without covariates; tau2_model = residual between-study variance with covariates.
notes: [R] Truncated at 0 when tau2_model > tau2_0. IHDChol (MM/DL): (0.0294 - 0.01647)/0.0294 = 43.97%, metareg's 'adjusted R-squared'. The book wrongly equates this with the WLS R^2. [note: imprecise with few studies, and the truncation at 0 hides negative values (López-López et al. 2014).]

name: Ordinary WLS R^2 (Stata regress)
expression: R^2 = SS_model / SS_total = mss / (mss + rss) = 1 - SS_res / SS_total
variables: mss = model (explained) weighted sum of squares; rss = residual weighted sum of squares.
notes: Example: 0.3736/(0.3736 + 1.1966) = 23.8%, adjusted 20.9%; 18.6% when the covariate is categorised. It is NOT the tau^2-based proportion of heterogeneity explained, although the book labels it that way.

name: Back-transformation of log-scale coefficients
expression: OR = exp(b) ;  CI = [ exp(b - crit*SE(b)) , exp(b + crit*SE(b)) ]
variables: b = coefficient or pooled estimate on the log scale; SE(b) = its standard error; crit = 1.96 (z) or the t quantile used by the model.
notes: Stata eform option. Example: robust slope exp(b) = 0.6217 per unit of cholesterol reduction, read as a 38% reduction in the odds.

name: Delta-method SE printed by Stata eform
expression: SE[exp(b)] ~= exp(b) * SE(b)
variables: b = log-scale coefficient; SE(b) = its standard error.
notes: A display convention: the 'Std. Err.' column of eform output is SE(exp b), not SE(b). Use SE(b) on the log scale for any further computation.

name: Variance of the reference category's log risk (cohort / RCT)
expression: var(theta_0) = 1/r_0 - 1/n_0
variables: r_0 = number of events in the reference category; n_0 = total in the reference category; theta_0 = log risk of the reference category.
notes: [R] Rebuilt from the fragments '1/r0 ... — 1/n0'; it matches the binomial variance of a log risk. It feeds the GLS covariance used by GLST. With confounder-adjusted RRs it is unavailable, so the covariance is 'somewhat biased'.

name: Variance of the reference category's log odds (case-control)
variables: r_0 = number of cases in the reference category; n_0 - r_0 = number of controls in the reference category.
notes: [R] Rebuilt from the fragment '1/r0 + 1/(n0 - r0)'; it matches the variance of a log odds.

name: GLST per-study model (stage 1) and pooling (stage 2)
expression: y_j = X_j beta_j + e_j ,  Cov(e_j) = C_j ;  beta_hat_j = (X_j' C_j^-1 X_j)^-1 X_j' C_j^-1 y_j ;  stage 2: multivariate FE/RE pooling of beta_hat_j
variables: y_j = vector of non-reference log RRs of study j; X_j = spline terms of the doses (NO intercept, so the curve passes through the origin); C_j = within-study covariance reconstructed from cases and group sizes (Greenland–Longnecker); beta_j = study coefficients.
notes: [ext] The book describes GLS and GLST in words only. Stata: glst logrr doses*, cov(person_years cases) se(se) pfirst(id studytype) r|f. The per-study coefficients in Table 13.3 reproduce only partly. Not implemented in the engine.

name: REMR one-stage weighted model
expression: y_ij = b0 + b1*s1(dose_ij) + b2*s2(dose_ij) + e_ij ;  w_ij = 1/se_ij^2 (non-reference rows) ;  w_0j = max_i w_ij (reference row) ;  WLS with cluster-robust SE (cluster = study)
variables: y_ij = log RR (or mean / MD) of category i in study j; s1, s2 = restricted cubic spline terms; se_ij = SE of y_ij; b0 = intercept (estimated, not forced to 0).
notes: Xu & Doi 2018. Stata: gen wt = 1/(se^2); bysort id: egen maxwt = max(wt); replace wt = maxwt if wt==.; regress logrr doses* [aweight=wt], vce(cluster id). Aripiprazole means: b1 = 1.017204, b2 = -0.7326656, b0 = 4.664162. Not implemented in the engine.

name: Restricted cubic spline basis (3 knots)
variables: x = dose; t1 < t2 < t3 = knot locations; s1 = linear term; s2 = cubic spline term.
notes: [ext] Stata mkspline ..., cubic basis; the book gives only the verbal definition (n knots give n - 1 terms; 3–7 knots typical). Stata's default nk(3) knots sit at the 10th/50th/90th percentiles, but the book's results need knots (0.97, 9.40, 22.86) for alcohol and (0, 10, 20) for aripiprazole.

name: One-stage centring of reference doses
expression: dosec_ij = dose_ij - dose_0j
variables: dose_ij = assigned dose of category i in study j; dose_0j = reference dose of study j; dosec = centred dose (common reference 0, a 'dose increment').
notes: Stata: sort id dose; bysort id: gen dosec = dose - dose[1]. The book notes that results then become harder to explain clinically.

name: Two-stage centring of reference doses
expression: dosec_ij = dose_ij - dose_0j + median_j( dose_0j )
variables: median_j(dose_0j) = median of the original reference doses across studies; other symbols as in one-stage centring.
notes: Book example: reference doses 1–3 with median 2 give bysort id: gen dosec = dose - dose[1] + 2. Use only when reference-dose differences are not substantial; otherwise exclude studies or do not pool.

name: Wald tests for spline dose-response models
expression: non-linearity: H0: beta_2 = ... = beta_(n-1) = 0 ;  association: H0: beta_1 = ... = beta_(n-1) = 0 ;  W = b_S' (V_S)^-1 b_S ~ chi2(|S|)  [or F = W/|S| with G - 1 denominator df after cluster-robust regress]
variables: n = number of knots; beta_1 = linear spline coefficient; beta_2..beta_(n-1) = cubic spline coefficients; S = tested subset; b_S, V_S = their estimates and covariance matrix.
notes: Stata: test doses2 (non-linearity), test doses1 doses2 (association). Recomputed: alcohol REMR non-linearity p = 0.2611 (printed 0.861 in Table 13.4, 0.261 in text); aripiprazole doses2 = 0 p = 0.0093 (the book's 0.0011 is the overall F(2,4) = 58.21). [note: the book's general sentence on p. 282 assigns coefficients 2..n-1 to the association test. Its example and code use all coefficients for association, as above.]

name: Dose-specific predicted effect and CI (xblc)
expression: REMR: y_hat(d) = b0 + b1*s1(d) + b2*s2(d) ;  GLST: y_hat(d) = b1*[s1(d) - s1(d_ref)] + b2*[s2(d) - s2(d_ref)] ;  SE = sqrt(x_d' V x_d) ;  RR(d) = exp(y_hat +/- 1.96*SE)
variables: d = dose of interest; d_ref = reference dose (ref(0) in xblc); x_d = design row at d; V = coefficient covariance; b0 = REMR intercept.
notes: xblc CIs are z-based and include the constant when the model has one. Hence REMR RR at dose 0 = 0.95 (0.86–1.04) instead of 1, and the aripiprazole MD at 15 mg/day = 10.55 (8.28–12.82) instead of 10.06 without b0. Use eform only for log-ratio outcomes.

name: Begg–Mazumdar rank correlation test
expression: t*_j = (theta_hat_j - theta_hat_FE) / sqrt(v*_j) ,  v*_j = v_j - 1/SUM w ;  test Kendall's tau between t*_j and v_j
variables: theta_hat_FE = fixed-effect estimate; v_j = within-study variance; w = 1/v; t*_j = standardised deviate.
notes: [ext, verified] Fibrinolysis 0.63 reproduces (exact and normal test agree). Magnesium 0.51 reproduces only on ln RR (0.5 zero-cell correction) with the normal approximation and no continuity correction (0.506). The engine, like metafor ranktest, uses the exact Kendall distribution and gives 0.534. Low power when k < 25. [note: the Cochrane Handbook v6 does not recommend Begg's test (low power).]

name: Egger's regression test
expression: theta_hat_j / SE_j = beta_0 + beta_1 * (1/SE_j) + e_j  (OLS) ;  H0: beta_0 = 0 ;  t with k - 2 df
variables: theta_hat_j / SE_j = standardised effect; 1/SE_j = precision; beta_0 = intercept (asymmetry).
notes: Asymmetry is declared at p < 0.10. Fibrinolysis p = 0.77; magnesium p < 0.001. Needs k >= 10; not for proportions. [note: for ln OR, Egger's test is anti-conservative because ln OR and its SE are correlated; for binary outcomes the Cochrane Handbook v6 prefers Harbord, Peters or Rücker. The 0.10 level is a convention, not a decision rule.]

name: Harbord's modified Egger test (binary outcomes)
expression: Z_j / sqrt(V_j) = beta_0 + beta_1 * sqrt(V_j) + e_j ;  Z = a - (a+b)(a+c)/N ;  V = (a+b)(c+d)(a+c)(b+d) / ( N^2 (N - 1) ) ;  H0: beta_0 = 0
variables: Z = efficient score of the log OR; V = its (score) variance; a, b, c, d = 2x2 cells; N = a + b + c + d.
notes: [ext] The book gives only the verbal form; the Z and V formulas are from Harbord et al. 2006. Needs 2x2 counts. Magnesium p < 0.001.

name: Peters' regression test
expression: ln OR_j = beta_0 + beta_1 * (1/N_j) + e_j ,  WLS weights w_j = 1 / ( 1/(a+c) + 1/(b+d) ) ;  H0: beta_1 = 0
variables: N_j = total sample size of study j; a + c = total events; b + d = total non-events.
notes: [ext] The weights and the test on the slope come from Peters et al. 2006 and Stata metabias; the book says only that ln OR is regressed on 1/N. Needs 2x2 counts. Magnesium p = 0.001: these weights give 0.0005, which rounds to 0.001, while metafor regtest(predictor = 'ninv') with inverse-variance weights gives 0.0016.

name: LFK index (Doi plot asymmetry)
expression: sort by theta_hat ;  N_j = 100*max(v)/v_j ;  MR_1 = N_1/2 , MR_j = MR_(j-1) + (N_(j-1) + N_j)/2 ;  pct_j = (MR_j - 0.5)/SUM N ;  Z_j = PHI^-1(pct_j) ;  m = argmin |Z_j| ;  LFK = 5/(2k) * SUM_j [ Z_j + (max Z - min Z)/(max(theta_hat - theta_hat_m) - min(theta_hat - theta_hat_m)) * (theta_hat_j - theta_hat_m) ]
variables: theta_hat_j = effect (log scale) of study j; v_j = its variance; N_j = pseudo-size; MR_j = mid-rank; Z_j = normal quantile (Doi-plot y-axis uses |Z_j|); m = tip study; k = number of studies.
notes: [ext, verified] The metasens::lfkindex algorithm; the book describes the index only in words. |LFK| <= 1 symmetry, 1–2 minor, > 2 major asymmetry. Fibrinolysis -0.6695 (book -0.67); magnesium -10.09 only with a 1.0 zero-cell correction (-10.27 with 0.5). [note: the developers' heuristic cut-offs; the index has no sampling distribution and is not endorsed by the Cochrane Handbook as a stand-alone test.]

name: Contour-enhanced funnel plot significance contours
expression: for each SE: theta_crit = +/- z_(1 - alpha/2) * SE  around the null (theta = 0 on the log scale) ,  alpha in {0.01, 0.05, 0.10}
variables: SE = standard error (funnel y-axis); z_(1-alpha/2) = 2.576, 1.960, 1.645; theta = effect on the log scale.
notes: [ext] The book only names the shaded regions (p < 0.01, < 0.05, < 0.1; Peters et al. 2008). The engine draws them with contour=True. Studies missing from the non-significant (white) area suggest publication bias.
